name: Uchar Waterfall
full: Uchar waterfall (cascade), also known as the Big Chulcha Waterfall — on the Chulcha River, a right tributary of the Chulyshman, in the Altai Nature Reserve
near: Koo village and the tourist bases of the Ak-Kurum tract in the Chulyshman valley; Balykcha village (south end of Lake Teletskoye)
elev: Cascade drop ≈160 m over a stream length of ≈600 m; the rock jam the river forces its way through is 300–350 m high (nature reserve); ascent on the trail ≈240 m (KP, 2026); absolute elevation of the foot — not found
short: The highest cascading waterfall in the Altai Republic (≈160 m): the Chulcha roars through a jam of giant boulders in a narrow canyon; you can get there only on foot — 8.5 km one way on a rocky trail with cables.
desc: Uchar (“impregnable” or “flying” in Altai language) is a cascading waterfall on the Chulcha River a few kilometers from where it joins the Chulyshman, in the Altai State Biosphere Reserve. The water drops about 160 m, passing for about 600 m through a pile of huge boulders; it is more of a chute than a sheer waterfall. The cascade is thought to have formed from a collapse after the strong earthquakes of the late 19th and early 20th centuries; it was first described by V. Vereshchagin (1905 diary) and scientifically surveyed in 1982. Today it is the reserve's eco-educational route “Uchar Chute”: 8.5 km one way (≈3.5 h from the crossing), linear, of moderate difficulty for prepared hikers; the most dangerous rock section (a narrow ledge above the river) is equipped with railings, cables and metal staples (via ferrata, built in 2014). The start is on the right bank of the Chulyshman, where you are ferried across by boat; before setting out you must check in at the seasonal registration point. In 2011 Uchar was among Russia's five hardest-to-reach sights; in 2014 about 2000 people visited it (against 40,000 for Korbu). The route usually opens after the spring flood, in June (in 2016, after 20 June); in 2026 it was closed on 17–20 August and from 31 August to the end of the season because of bears.
guide: Uchar is for those who find viewing platforms too little: you walk 3–4 hours through the taiga along the Chulyshman and the Chulcha, scramble over staples above the river, and at the end you hear a roar so loud you can't hear your neighbor. Set out at first light so you can get back to the boat before dark — the whole hike takes 7–8 hours. Locals joke about the “ground bunnies” — the chipmunks that steal food at rest stops — so don't leave your backpack open. Bring shoes with grippy soles: wet logs and rocks are the main enemy. On the way, look in at the Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms — they are almost opposite.
see: The cascade itself with the viewpoint at its foot; the Chulcha canyon; the cable-equipped ledge above the river; views of the Chulyshman valley; along the way, the taiga and the mouth of the Chulcha
skip: you aren't ready for 17 km on foot there and back over rocks and staples, are afraid of heights, or are traveling with small children — in that case stick to the Stone Mushrooms and Katu-Yaryk
diff: Moderate to high: 8.5 km one way, a rock ledge with cables and staples, fords/logs; good physical fitness required
when: Late June to September (after the flood, when the reserve opens the route); May–June has the most water, but the trail is often closed because of floods and rockfalls
hours: The reserve route is seasonal — June to September (English page of the reserve), in daylight; limit of up to 4 groups a day of 10–15 people, groups with an accompanying instructor, registration at the point at the start of the trail. In 2026: closed 17–20.08, then from 20.08 “until further notice” (bears on the trail), and from 31.08 all the reserve's routes are closed until the end of the season
daytime: An early start (7–8 am), at the waterfall around noon, when the sun looks into the canyon
how: First, get to the Chulyshman valley, to the tourist bases of the Ak-Kurum tract / Koo village. Option 1 (overland): Chuysky Trakt to Aktash → Ulagan → Balyktuyul → Katu-Yaryk Pass → down the valley to about km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road (≈100 km from Aktash to the pass + ≈30 km along the valley), 4×4 / SUV only. Option 2 (by water): a car ferry or motorboat from Artybash to the south end of Lake Teletskoye (5–6 h), then by car/UAZ up the valley. Then by boat across the Chulyshman to the right bank and 8.5 km on foot along the trail beside the Chulcha. From Artybash in one day — only on tours (12 h, but such tours usually include the Stone Mushrooms rather than Uchar).
needcar: Yes — a 4×4 / SUV or a ferry/motorboat to the valley, plus a boat crossing over the Chulyshman; the trail itself is on foot only
self: Getting to the valley and crossing — yes. But the reserve's rules (English version of the site) require groups to go with an accompanying instructor and limit the flow to 4 groups a day; in practice solo travelers join a guide's group from a tourist base (≈1000 ₽/person, KP 2026). Registration at the point by the trail is mandatory
roadtype: To the valley — dirt/gravel and the Katu-Yaryk serpentine; the trail is a rocky mountain path with a rock ledge, cables and staples
traveltime: Trail ≈3.5–4 h one way, 7–8 h for everything including sightseeing; Aktash → Ak-Kurum ≈4–5 h by 4×4 / SUV (estimate); ferry Artybash → south end 5–6 h
stay: Tourist bases and campsites of the Ak-Kurum tract (km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road): Dolina Vodopadov (from 3000 ₽, 4.9/67 on 2GIS), Dolina Kamennykh Gribov (from 4500 ₽, 4.8/99), Kamennye Griby (from 2500 ₽, 4.3/79; yurt from 350 ₽ — mirturbaz); Zolotaya Dolina Chulyshmana (Koo, from 2500–3000 ₽); tents from 100 ₽/person (KP, 2026)
net: There is no mobile signal in the valley according to KP (2026); according to T—Zh (2025) it has appeared but is unstable; on the trail — none. Some tourist bases have Wi-Fi (satellite/generators)
entry: Altai Nature Reserve route ticket: 250 ₽/person (since 27.02.2025, all eco-educational routes); older sources say 100–180 ₽ (KP gives 100 ₽ for 2026 — contradictory). No border-zone permit needed.
transfer: Boat across the Chulyshman 1000 ₽ per boat of up to 4 people round trip (2026) / 1500 ₽ at the campsite; previously ≈500 ₽/person (KP); transfer Ulagan → valley 16,000 ₽ for up to 8 people (2026); car ferry 15–17k ₽ (2026)
bring: Trekking shoes with grippy soles, gloves for the cables, 1.5–2 L of water, a snack, a rain jacket, repellent and tick protection, a headlamp, a first-aid kit
warn: In 2026 the trail has been closed since 20.08 “until further notice”: bears have appeared on it, and even inspectors are barred from access (reserve, Altapress 08.2026); from 31.08 all the reserve's routes are closed. The rock ledge above the river — hold on to the cables; setting out in rain is forbidden (mudflows). The most serious crossing is the Artyshtu stream. In spring (May–June) there are floods, mudflows and rockfalls, and the route is closed. Heat in the canyon above +30 °C. Ticks. No signal — guides carry satellite phones. No border-zone permit needed
food: Meals at the Ak-Kurum tourist bases (dinner for two from 1300 ₽, KP 2026); a cafe at Chulyshmanskaya Berezka by the crossing; fish soup and fried grayling/roach caught in the Chulyshman
reviews: No rating for the waterfall itself was found on 2GIS/Yandex. Tourist bases at the start of the trail: Dolina Vodopadov 4.9 (67), Dolina Kamennykh Gribov 4.8 (99) on 2GIS. Pros: the power of the cascade, wild taiga, few people; cons: a hard trail, slippery rocks, seasonal closures, the road over Katu-Yaryk.
photos.0.cap: Big Chulcha Waterfall (Uchar) on the Chulcha River
p.sum: Uchar is a day hike (≈17 km round trip, 7–8 h) from the tourist bases of the Ak-Kurum tract in the Chulyshman valley: a boat across the river (≈500 ₽), registration, the reserve ticket (250 ₽, 2025). To reach the valley: over Katu-Yaryk by 4×4 / SUV, or by ferry/motorboat across Teletskoye. Stay overnight at the Ak-Kurum tourist bases (from 2500–4500 ₽ per cabin) or at a campsite (from 100 ₽/person). In 2026 the trail has been closed since 20 August because of bears.

p.permits: No border-zone permit needed (Ulagan district is not on the list of Altai Republic border zones). A reserve route ticket and registration at the seasonal point; organized groups must apply to the reserve (tel. +7 38822 2-14-19). Under reserve rules groups go with an accompanying instructor, limit 4 groups/day of 10–15 people; setting out in rain is forbidden; in 2026 the trail has been closed since 20.08.
p.access: Not for young children, older people or those with limited mobility (the trail is not adapted). Dogs are probably not allowed in the reserve (not confirmed).
